name: GarminMetrics
title: Garmin metrics without a standard code
description: Codes for Garmin Connect measurements that have no correct LOINC code. Values that do have one (heart rate, steps, sleep durations, SpO2, weight and others) use LOINC instead; see docs/fhir-mapping.md. Each concept states its unit, scale and the Garmin field it comes from. Group concepts are not selectable and only organise the codes.

property.description: Group concept; never used as an Observation code.
UCUM unit the value is recorded in. Absent for text values.
FHIR value type used: Quantity, SampledData or CodeableConcept (text only).
Source file and JSON path in the raw archive.

concept.definition: Whole-day movement totals that have no matching LOINC code.
Calories burned above resting metabolism during the calendar day, estimated by Garmin from heart rate and movement.
Calories Garmin attributes to basal metabolism for the calendar day, estimated from age, sex, height and weight. Not a measured resting metabolic rate.
Number of floors (about 3 m of altitude each, from the barometer) walked down during the calendar day.
The step target Garmin set for that day (auto goal or user set). A goal, not a measurement.
The floors-climbed target for that day. A goal, not a measurement.
Weekly target for intensity minutes, where vigorous minutes count double. A goal, not a measurement.
Heart-rate statistics that have no matching LOINC code.
Average of the daily resting heart rate over the 7 days ending on this day, as calculated by Garmin.

Garmin stress score. Calculated by the watch from heart-rate variability while the wearer is not moving. Scale 0-100: 0-25 rest, 26-50 low, 51-75 medium, 76-100 high. Not a psychological or self-reported stress measure, so LOINC 93038-8 'Stress level' does not apply.
Average Garmin stress score (0-100) over the measured part of the day. Lower is more relaxed.
Highest Garmin stress score (0-100) of the day.
Time during the day with a stress score of 0-25.
Time during the day with a stress score of 26-50.
Time during the day with a stress score of 51-75.
Time during the day with a stress score of 76-100.

concept.display: Time too active to measure stress
concept.definition: Time during the day when movement prevented a stress reading.
Time during the day with no stress reading, for example when the watch was off the wrist.
Garmin's one-word label for the day's stress, as text, for example 'balanced'.

Garmin Body Battery: a proprietary 0-100 estimate of energy reserves, calculated from heart-rate variability, stress, sleep and activity. Higher means more energy in reserve. It has no clinical equivalent.
Body Battery value (0-100) at a point in time.
Highest Body Battery value (0-100) of the calendar day, usually just after waking.
Lowest Body Battery value (0-100) of the calendar day.
Body Battery value (0-100) at the end of the calendar day, or at the last sync for a day still in progress.

concept.display: Body Battery charged during the day
concept.definition: Total points gained during the calendar day, mostly during sleep and rest.

concept.display: Body Battery drained during the day
concept.definition: Total points lost during the calendar day, from activity and stress.

concept.display: Body Battery change during an event
concept.definition: Points gained (positive) or lost (negative) during one event such as a night's sleep or a workout.
Kind of event as Garmin labels it, as text, for example 'SLEEP'.

Overnight heart-rate variability measured by the Garmin wrist sensor. Garmin reports RMSSD (root mean square of successive differences between R-R intervals). LOINC 80404-7 and 112429-6 are SDNN, a different statistic, so they must not be used for these values.
Average RMSSD during the sleep that ends on this calendar day. Higher is generally better, but compare with the person's own baseline rather than with other people.
Highest 5-minute RMSSD average during that sleep.
Average of the nightly RMSSD values over the last 7 nights.
Personal baseline from Garmin: 7-day averages below this are 'low'.
Personal baseline from Garmin: lower end of the balanced range.
Personal baseline from Garmin: upper end of the balanced range.
Garmin's label comparing the 7-day average with the baseline, as text: BALANCED, UNBALANCED, LOW, POOR or NONE.
RMSSD values every 5 minutes during sleep, as a time series.
Sleep values from the Garmin wrist sensor that have no matching LOINC code. The sleep belongs to the calendar day on which it ends.
Total daytime nap time attributed to the day.
Time in the sleep window that the watch could not classify.
Times the wearer woke during the sleep window.
Average Garmin stress score (0-100) during sleep.
Average heart rate during sleep.
Average breaths per minute during sleep.
Lowest breaths per minute during sleep.
Highest breaths per minute during sleep.
Average blood-oxygen saturation during sleep, from the wrist pulse oximeter.
Lowest blood-oxygen saturation during sleep.
How much sleep Garmin recommended for this night, adjusted for HRV, recent sleep and training.
Garmin's overall sleep score, 0-100. Higher is better. Not comparable with questionnaire-based sleep scores such as LOINC 97891-6.
Garmin's label for the sleep score, as text: EXCELLENT, GOOD, FAIR or POOR.

concept.display: Deep sleep, share of total sleep
concept.definition: Deep sleep as a percentage of total sleep time.

concept.display: Light sleep, share of total sleep
concept.definition: Light sleep as a percentage of total sleep time.

concept.display: REM sleep, share of total sleep
concept.definition: REM sleep as a percentage of total sleep time.
Garmin's label for total sleep time, as text.
Garmin's label for the deep sleep share, as text.
Garmin's label for the light sleep share, as text.
Garmin's label for the REM sleep share, as text.
Garmin's label for movement during sleep, as text.
Garmin's label for the number of awakenings, as text.
Garmin's label for stress during sleep, as text.
Daily SpO2 and respiration statistics that have no matching LOINC code. Measured by the wrist pulse oximeter; less accurate than a clinical finger oximeter.
Lowest blood-oxygen reading of the calendar day.
Lowest breaths per minute of the calendar day.
Highest breaths per minute of the calendar day.
Garmin fitness age: an estimate of the age the person's fitness corresponds to, from resting heart rate, BMI and vigorous activity. Lower than the real age is better.
Garmin's estimated fitness age in years.
Fitness age Garmin estimates the person could reach by meeting its targets.

concept.display: Vigorous activity days per week, 6-week average
concept.definition: Average number of days per week with vigorous activity, used by fitness age.
Average vigorous-activity minutes per week, used by fitness age.
Values for one recorded workout (activity) that have no matching LOINC code. The full per-second recording is in the attached FIT file.
Distance covered during the workout.
Time from start to end, pauses included.
Time spent moving.
Steps taken during the workout.
Distance divided by timer time.
Highest speed recorded.
Average speed corrected for uphill and downhill, as the equivalent speed on flat ground.
Total climb during the workout.
Total descent during the workout.
Average running or cycling power.
Highest power recorded.
Power adjusted for variability, approximating the physiological cost of the effort.
Average steps per minute.
Highest steps per minute.
Average length of one step.
Average time each foot is on the ground per step.
Average up-and-down movement of the torso per step.
Vertical oscillation divided by stride length. Lower is more efficient.
Garmin's 0.0-5.0 estimate of the workout's effect on aerobic fitness.
Garmin's 0.0-5.0 estimate of the workout's effect on anaerobic capacity.
Garmin's label for the main benefit, as text, for example 'AEROBIC_BASE'.
Garmin's estimate of the workout's physiological load (EPOC-based).

concept.display: Body Battery change during the workout
concept.definition: Body Battery points gained or lost during the workout. Usually negative.
Garmin's estimated stamina at the start, 0-100.
Garmin's estimated stamina at the end, 0-100.
Garmin's estimate of the mechanical load on the body from foot strikes.
How the workout felt, entered by the user on the watch: 0 very weak, 25 weak, 50 normal, 75 strong, 100 very strong.
Perceived exertion entered by the user, stored by Garmin as 10-100 (10 times the 1-10 RPE scale).
Garmin's estimate of fluid lost during the workout.
Time spent in heart-rate zone 1 (warm up), using the zones in effect when recorded.
Time spent in heart-rate zone 2 (easy).
Time spent in heart-rate zone 3 (aerobic).
Time spent in heart-rate zone 4 (threshold).
Time spent in heart-rate zone 5 (maximum).
Time spent in power zone 1.
Time spent in power zone 2.
Time spent in power zone 3.
Time spent in power zone 4.
Time spent in power zone 5.
